w:r.w:t: The Information Architecture of the proposed Curriculum Management System organizes all academic structures, operational workspaces, and administrative workflows into a transparent, multi-level hierarchy. As illustrated in Figure 3.1, the architecture establishes a direct vertical continuum—guiding authorized institutional users from high-level institutional governance down to granular course specifications and prerequisite dependencies. This deliberate organization prevents visual clutter, minimizes cognitive friction, and establishes dedicated functional zones tailored to the operational responsibilities of academic leaders, curriculum designers, and instructional faculty.

At the summit of the hierarchy sits the System Authentication Portal and Institutional Dashboard. Users authenticate using their institutional email credentials, which resolves role-specific security permissions. Upon verified entry, users land on the Institutional Dashboard, which serves as the primary institutional overview. The dashboard summarizes active academic divisions, degree offerings, and overall curricular compliance metrics. Authorized academic leaders can review school health or provision new academic units through guided administrative controls.

Selecting an academic school transitions the interface into the School Overview tier (e.g., School of Engineering). This level consolidates all degree programs administered by the school, displaying leadership credentials, executive director profiles, and institutional accreditation standings. From this directory, selecting an individual academic program transitions the workspace into the Program Overview tier.

The Program Overview tier (e.g., Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering) coordinates program-level parameters, accreditation rubrics, and degree requirements. Within this tier, users can inspect active, draft, and historical curriculum version batches (such as Academic Year 2025-2026). While courses and syllabi represent essential building blocks, the functional core of the platform is situated within the Curriculum Management Level.

The Curriculum Management Level acts as the central workbench for curriculum authoring, outcomes alignment, and institutional compliance governance. It brings together five tightly coupled operational pillars: (1) Curriculum Version Histories, enabling academic heads to evaluate historical baselines, author new academic batches, and freeze approved revisions across batch registries (such as CM-BSCpE-2026 and historical cohorts CPE2023–CPE2027), along with registries for Student Outcomes, Program Educational Objectives, Graduate Attributes, and Institutional Mission, Vision, and Values; (2) Curriculum Mapping, coordinating multi-tier outcomes alignment across institutional competencies; (3) Task Delegations, enabling time-bound, cluster-specific editing privileges for instructional faculty; (4) System Audit Logs, capturing chronological, immutable activity records for institutional accreditation oversight; and (5) Batch Data Tools, supporting automated Excel (.xlsx) matrix ingestion and encrypted institutional JSON backups.

Under any selected Curriculum Version (e.g., AY 2025-2026 v1 / CM-BSCpE-2026), the architecture exposes five integrated analytical subsystems arranged in dedicated operational columns: (1) Curriculum Map (OBE Alignment Hub), coordinating the four-tier outcomes hierarchy from Graduate Attributes down to course competencies, complete with the Course-to-SO matrix (I-P-D), SO-to-PEO alignment schedule, and PEO-to-GA matrix; (2) Interactive Flowchart, visualizing the curriculum as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) across 12 trimesters with real-time prerequisite validation, course node inspector/editor modal, and Obsidian Gold high-contrast dark mode; (3) Master Spreadsheet, delivering a live editable 74-course catalog grid with formula bar, Lecture/Laboratory unit separation, and instant credit summation; (4) Official Documents Suite, rendering publication-ready registrar records (Sheets 1 to 7: Course Catalog, Curriculum Flowchart, Comparative Summary, Program of Study, Prospectus, Summary of Units, and OBE Mapping Sheet) formatted strictly for standard paper; and (5) Curriculum Dashboard, providing real-time compliance analytics, verifying the 172.0 total credit unit requirement, conducting the CHED CMO No. 92 Series of 2017 audit checklist, monitoring 13/13 Student Outcomes coverage, and tracking the three specialized elective tracks.

Complementing the analytical views is the comprehensive Outcomes-Based Education (OBE) mapping engine. This subsystem enforces a strict four-tier alignment tree: Graduate Attributes (GA 2024, 9 institutional attributes) map directly to Program Educational Objectives (PEO 2026, 5 program objectives), which decompose into Student Outcomes (SO 2026, 13 outcomes a through m grounded in CHED CMO No. 92), which then link to individual courses designated by Introduced (I), Practiced (P), and Demonstrated (D) competency levels. This guarantees complete transparency from institutional vision down to classroom assessment.

The Navigation Structure outlines the pathways through which academic personnel interact with system modules. As detailed in Figure 3.2, the structure mirrors the Information Architecture through a dual-navigation paradigm: a persistent Left Navigation Sidebar that functions as an institutional file-explorer tree enabling direct random-access hopping across academic schools, degree programs, curriculum cohorts (e.g., CPE2027 draft, CPE2026 active baseline, historical archives), and governance tools; and a progressive main-canvas drilldown supported by contextual breadcrumbs, a zero-reload top view-switcher, modal overlays, and explicit return paths at every level.

Users commence navigation at the Login Screen by providing institutional credentials. Successful authentication routes the user directly to the Institutional Dashboard. If credentials fail verification, an error prompt is displayed and the user remains at the login portal. From the Dashboard, users can branch into academic schools or initiate a session termination via the Logout action.

Selecting the School of Engineering navigates to the School Overview, presenting all constituent programs. Choosing Computer Engineering moves navigation into the Program Overview. From here, users transition directly into the Curriculum Management Home Page, the operational core of the platform.

From the Curriculum Management Home Page, selecting an active curriculum version (e.g., AY 2025-2026 v1 / CM-BSCpE-2026) unlocks the primary analytical workspaces through a persistent top navigation view-switcher. Users can transition with zero reloading delay between five specialized views: Curriculum Dashboard, Interactive Flowchart, Master Spreadsheet, Curriculum Map (OBE Alignment Hub), and the Official Documents publication suite.

The Flowchart view allows users to pan, zoom, and inspect course nodes and prerequisite links, opening the Course Details modal on demand for modifying requisites, unit distributions, and course metadata. The Spreadsheet view provides a high-density editable grid with formula bar for updating course codes, credit units, and prerequisites with instant validation. The Curriculum Map view exposes interactive tabs for exploring the outcomes hierarchy, the Course-to-SO matrix (I-P-D), the SO-to-PEO schedule, and the PEO-to-GA matrix. The Curriculum Dashboard delivers real-time compliance health, auditing CHED CMO No. 92 standards and unit totals.

The Official Documents module provides direct navigation across seven standardized registrar sheets: Course Catalog, Curriculum Flowchart, Comparative Summary, Program of Study, Student Prospectus, Summary of Units, and OBE Mapping Sheet. Each format offers print-ready previews formatted for US Letter / A4 paper with one-click PDF generation. Administrative navigation controls allow authorized personnel to access the Versioning History registries, collaborative Task Delegation console, immutable System Audit Trail, and Batch Data Ingestion/Export modals.

Administrative navigation paths allow authorized Program Directors to open the Task Delegation console and assign temporary, cluster-specific editing privileges to faculty members. The Audit Log screen provides a searchable, filterable activity history recording timestamps, user accounts, actions performed, and affected curriculum records.

To ensure user freedom, return navigation paths are provided at every level. Users can return from operational tools back to the Curriculum Management Home Page, from Curriculum Management to the Program Overview, and from the Program Overview back to the Dashboard. Role-based visibility ensures that controls requiring elevated administrative privileges are visible only to authorized personnel.

The navigation structure also considers the permissions assigned to each user. Functions that require specific permissions are only available to authorized users, supporting role-based navigation throughout the system. The complete navigation structure is shown in

The User Flow illustrates the sequence of actions performed by users when completing major tasks within the proposed Curriculum Management System. Each flow begins with the user's entry into the system and shows the actions, system responses, and outcome of the task. The User Flow is based on the system's main functions and the responsibilities of authorized users.

The user begins by accessing the Login page and entering their email and password. The system verifies the credentials and, when valid, directs the user to the Dashboard. If the credentials are invalid, the system displays an error message and allows the user to try again.
Figure 3.4. School and Program Management Flow

From the Dashboard, the user can select an existing school or, if authorized, add a new school by entering the school name, Executive Director, and programs offered. After selecting a school, the user accesses the School Overview, where programs can be added or edited. Program information includes the program name and Program Director. Selecting a program directs the user to the Program Overview.

From the Program Overview, the user selects Curriculum Management. The Curriculum Management Home Page provides access to Curriculum Versions, Delegations, and Audit Logs. When managing curriculum versions, the user can select an existing version, create a new version, or add a revision.

After selecting a curriculum version, the user can access the Flowchart, Spreadsheet, or Official Documents. In the Flowchart, authorized users can arrange subjects and select individual courses to edit details such as the course name, course code, units, year level, prerequisites, and other course information. When configuring prerequisites, the system automatically checks for circular dependencies to ensure that prerequisite chains remain valid. After making changes, the user can save the updated curriculum.
Figure 3.7. Curriculum Spreadsheet and Mapping Flow

The user can also access the Spreadsheet, where curriculum information can be used for I/E/D mapping and the generation of summaries or reports. Authorized users can update the required information and save the changes. The updated information can be exported for further use.

The Official Documents section allows users to view the imported documents associated with the selected curriculum version. Changes made to the curriculum through the Flowchart or Spreadsheet are reflected in the corresponding document information according to the system's document management process.
Figure 3.9. Data Import and Export Flow

The system also allows users to import existing Excel files and export updated curriculum data. Users can import existing information, review or modify the data, save the changes, and export the updated information for reuse or further editing.

For Curriculum Mapping, the user accesses the module from the Curriculum Management Home Page and selects the mapping component to manage. The module organizes the mapping relationships among Graduate Attributes (GAs), Program Educational Objectives (PEOs), Student Outcomes (SOs), and courses. A PEO can be mapped to its corresponding Graduate Attribute or Attributes, while an SO can be mapped to its corresponding PEO or PEOs. Courses can then be mapped to the appropriate Student Outcomes. This establishes the mapping relationship from the course level to the SO, from the SO to the PEO, and from the PEO to the Graduate Attribute.

Authorized users can create or edit Graduate Attributes, PEOs, and SOs and maintain their corresponding mappings. For course mapping, the user selects a course from the selected curriculum version, views its current SO mappings, and adds, modifies, or removes the appropriate SO mappings. The system saves the updated mapping information after the changes are completed.

For Delegations, an authorized user accesses the Delegations section from the Curriculum Management Home Page, selects a curriculum-related task, and assigns it to a Faculty member. Temporary privileges are provided to allow the Faculty member to complete the assigned task. The system records the activity performed during the delegated task.

For Audit Logs, an authorized user accesses the Audit Logs from the Curriculum Management Home Page and reviews recorded activities. Each record displays information such as when the activity occurred, who performed the action, what action was performed, and the associated ID number.

The high-fidelity user interface represents the fully implemented, production-ready graphical presentation of the Centralized Curriculum Management System. Built upon Asia Pacific College's institutional visual identity—featuring APC Navy Blue (#002855), APC Gold (#E5A823), and clean surface neutrals—the interface integrates fluid responsive typography, clear interactive signifiers, and rich tabular layouts. The following twenty-four screens showcase the live operational state of the platform across all administrative, curricular, and audit modules.
Figure 3.37. Authentication and Role-Based Login Screen

The Authentication and Role-Based Login screen presents an institutional login modal overlaid on the Asia Pacific College brand palette. It enforces strict credential validation via institutional email accounts (@apc.edu.ph), initializing role-tailored security permissions for Program Directors, Faculty Members, and Academic Administrators.

The Institutional Dashboard screen provides an executive summary of academic performance across the institution. High-level metric cards display active degree programs, total curricular units (184 units for Computer Engineering), and real-time compliance with CHED CMO No. 92, Series of 2017. Navigation buttons provide immediate access to constituent schools and program registries.

The School Overview screen organizes degree programs under the School of Engineering. It displays executive leadership credentials, degree program listings, and accreditation levels. Quick-action buttons allow academic heads to drill into program catalogs or provision new program offerings.

The Degree Program Management screen provides a catalog of engineering programs including Computer Engineering (BSCpE), Electronics Engineering (BSECE), and Civil Engineering (BSCE). Each entry highlights degree code, academic leadership, active batch year, and launch buttons leading into the dedicated Curriculum Workbench.

The Curriculum Workbench Overview screen serves as the primary authoring and analysis workspace for a selected curriculum version (such as AY 2025-2026 v1). It consolidates access to the four core analytical modules—Flowchart, Spreadsheet, OBE Engine, and Official Documents—along with version control locks and revision triggers.

The Interactive Curriculum Flowchart screen visualizes the curriculum structure as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Courses are organized across four academic years and three trimesters per year, with distinct category color coding. Clicking any node illuminates its upstream prerequisites and downstream dependent courses while launching the course details modal.

The Course Details Modal and Inspector screen provides a focused dialog for viewing and editing course attributes. It details course code, descriptive title, lecture units, lab units, total credit units, prerequisite chains, and corequisite linkages, ensuring consistent validation across both flowchart and spreadsheet representations.

The Curriculum Spreadsheet Data Grid screen delivers a high-density, live-editable tabular interface. It supports in-cell data entry, column sorting, category filtering, and automated credit unit summation per trimester. Edits made in the spreadsheet immediately propagate to the interactive flowchart and official registrar documents.

The Outcomes-Based Education (OBE) Hierarchy Hub screen organizes institutional learning outcomes into structured tiers. It illustrates the alignment progression from APC Graduate Attributes (GAs) to Program Educational Objectives (PEOs), Student Outcomes (SOs), and Course Outcomes (COs), ensuring full alignment with accreditation requirements.

OBE Course-to-SO Matrix Screen: The Course-to-Student Outcomes (I-E-D) Matrix screen renders the complete curriculum competency mapping table. Every course in the degree program is evaluated against the 13 student outcomes using Introduced (I), Enabling (E), and Demonstrative (D) classifications, complete with row-level validation ensuring that senior capstone courses demonstrate all required outcomes.
Figure 3.47. OBE SO-to-PEO Alignment Schedule Screen

The Student Outcomes to Program Educational Objectives (SO-PEO) Alignment Schedule screen establishes direct links between measurable student capabilities upon graduation and long-term career achievements. The matrix confirms that each engineering outcome reinforces at least one institutional educational objective.

The PEO to Graduate Attributes (GA) Alignment screen connects program objectives to the foundational core attributes of Asia Pacific College graduates, including Professional Competence, Critical Thinking, Ethical Responsibility, and Lifelong Learning.
Figure 3.49. Official Course Catalog Document Screen

The Official Document 1: Course Catalog screen provides a publication-grade, printable document formatted strictly for standard US Letter paper. It presents an alphabetized and categorized inventory of all accredited courses, showing course codes, complete descriptive titles, unit loads, and prerequisite requirements.
Figure 3.50. Official Curriculum Flowchart Document Screen

The Official Document 2: Curriculum Flowchart Document screen formats the complete curriculum map into a clean, black-and-white grid approved for registrar publication and academic advising. It includes formal signatory spaces for the Program Director, Executive Director, and Registrar.
Figure 3.51. Official Comparative Summary Report Screen

The Official Document 3: Comparative Summary Report screen renders a side-by-side delta analysis between the previous curriculum baseline and the revised curriculum version. It categorizes unit variances across General Education, Professional Core, Electives, and On-the-Job Training.
Figure 3.52. Official Program of Study Sheet Screen
Official Program of Study Sheet Screen:

The Official Document 4: Program of Study Sheet screen formats the prescribed four-year academic roadmap into sequential trimester blocks. Each term details course offerings, contact hours, lecture/lab splits, credit units, and prerequisite prerequisites required for enrollment.

The Official Document 5: Student Prospectus Sheet screen delivers an individual academic evaluation checklist. Designed for student tracking and graduation audits, it records course grades, completion terms, and accredited status alongside official institution seals.
Figure 3.54. Batch Excel Data Ingestion Modal Screen
Batch Excel Data Ingestion Modal Screen:

The Batch Excel Data Ingestion Modal screen provides an automated pipeline for uploading existing departmental curriculum spreadsheets (.xlsx). The interface validates column headers, checks data formats, detects missing prerequisites, and stages data for user review prior to database commit.
Figure 3.55. Data Export and Institutional Backup Modal Screen
Data Export and Institutional Backup Modal Screen:

The Data Export and Institutional Backup Modal screen allows administrators to download complete curriculum snapshots in multiple open formats, including structured JSON archives, multi-tab Excel workbooks, and combined registrar-approved PDF dossiers.
Figure 3.56. Collaborative Task Delegation Console Screen

The Collaborative Task Delegation Console screen empowers Program Directors to assign time-bound editing privileges to specialized faculty members. Delegations are scoped to specific course clusters (such as Software Engineering or Hardware Systems), ensuring collaborative authoring while safeguarding institutional curriculum governance.
Figure 3.57. Immutable System Audit Trail Screen

The Immutable System Audit Trail screen provides a tamper-evident chronological ledger tracking all administrative actions within the platform. Recorded attributes include exact ISO timestamps, user identity, action type, affected curriculum version, and before/after delta states.
Figure 3.58. System Preferences and Settings Modal Screen
System Preferences and Settings Modal Screen:

The System Preferences and Settings Modal screen provides institutional configuration options, including trimester scheduling definitions, default academic year baselines, auto-save interval settings (default 30 seconds), and role privilege hierarchies.
Figure 3.59. Obsidian Gold Dark Mode Flowchart Screen
Obsidian Gold Dark Mode Flowchart Screen:

The Obsidian Gold High-Contrast Dark Mode Screen renders the complete curriculum flowchart against deep charcoal and obsidian backgrounds with gold accent highlights. This mode meets WCAG AAA contrast standards and minimizes eye fatigue during extended curriculum review.
Figure 3.60. Curriculum Version History and Revision Log Screen
Curriculum Version History and Revision Log Screen:

The Curriculum Version History and Revision Log screen maintains a complete timeline of curriculum iterations across academic years. Users can inspect historical revisions, review change summaries, compare baseline diffs, and restore prior approved states if required.

The user interface of the website has been personally customized to cater to majority of the users. The elements of each website page has been scaled to take the attention of the users fairly easily to capture their attention for major parts of the navigation. For example, the home page banner would be the first things users would see, not only because that it is eye-level to the users being on the top of the website, but it also serves as a greeting for the users to the website.

The layout of the website is also consistent in terms of its scaling, spacing, and placement. The buttons appear uniform for each section of navigation through the management system. An example of this would be the buttons that lead the users from process-to-process. Each of these buttons displays the brief information the user needs for certain schools, programs, or courses (such as those seen from the School Page, Program Page, and the Curriculum Management page showcasing all active curricula). The spacing of the elements in each page follows a header-workspace margin to help users further separate the main work area from other parts of the UI.

To ensure readability and accessibility, one feature of the website includes the directory tree, allowing for an easier navigation tool for the users to quickly access the website page or file they need. Each website also comes with a back button for users to go back to the previous branch from the directory tree. Each clickable button is designed to catch the attention of the users with bold highlighted text and a border that allows a clear understanding for the user to signify the clickability of the button.

In relation to system feedback, the user interface makes it evident for any missing or improper inputs such as highlighting any missing or empty sections. The user interface makes it easy for the users to find exactly what they need when editing, inputting or submitting any requirement. This is also evident with the different roles and how the website responds depending on the user type (Admin, Executive, Program Director, or Faculty). The user roles works in an umbrella system which also works in tandem to the user interface; any accessibility roles works with the role above it (e.g. If Executives can edit certain course details, so can the Admin).
